- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; if price rises >5% from prior day, cap forecast increase at 3–5% to avoid overshoot.
- In 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong upward moves; if 3–5 consecutive days above 75, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next period.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.3, -0.5, +0.4), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more in 3 consecutive days); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for uncertainty.
